_comment: klt erc supply spec for the composed+ routed `pll_divider_chain` GDS of the
SG13CMOS5L PLL port -- the T1 item 11 (power delivery, structural) artifact
for this repo, per 2AMLogic/sg13g2-pll#103 and the upstream ladder item
(klayout-tools docs/design-evidence-tiers.md, approved as #2025).
Run it against the committed divider-chain layout of record
`reports/20260830-204105-457cf5b` (the current LATEST record):
klt erc layout/sg13cmos5l-pll/reports/20260830-204105-457cf5b/pll_divider_chain.gds \
layout/sg13cmos5l-pll/erc-supply-spec.json --format json
Pass conditions this spec grades (per #103, mirroring the upstream item
text): every declared supply resolves to exactly ONE electrical island --
no `erc.unconnected_net` (fires on zero matches AND on more than one, so a
zero count IS the one-island verdict, not merely an absence) and no
`erc.supply_short` naming it. An antenna verdict or a floating-gate finding
in the same report is a real defect but is NOT this item's subject and
does not block it (klayout-tools#1994). `erc.missing_tie` is NOT COMPUTED
by this run -- see the `ties[]` note below.
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- `stackup[0]` is `GatPoly` (5/0) with `role: "gate"` (klt erc's own
contract). `active_layer` (1/0, `Activ`) makes gate identification and
the antenna-ratio denominator `poly ∩ diff` rather than raw poly area
(klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate area: poly ∩ diff'), which is what
excludes the poly interconnect stubs this flow deliberately draws
(cmos5l_devices.py draws source/gate landing pads whose poly extends
past the diffusion) from `gates[]`, so they conduct (GatPoly is a real
wire role in the model) but are not graded as transistor gates.
- Metal1/Metal2/Metal3 are the only metal levels this block actually
routes supplies on, so they are the only metal roles declared:
cmos5l_route.py draws one vertical Metal2 riser per terminal, one
horizontal Metal3 trunk per net, Via1 between terminal pad and riser
and Via2 between riser and trunk; device terminals, the pfet row's
n-well tap and the nfet row's substrate tap all land on Metal1 pads.
No Metal4/Metal5 geometry exists in this GDS at all (verified by
`klt layers --flattened`: layer set is exactly 1/0, 5/0, 6/0, 7/0,
declaring them would contribute nothing.
- `Cont` (6/0) bridges GatPoly <-> Metal1, `Via1` (19/0) Metal1<->Metal2
and `Via2` (29/0) Metal2<->Metal3 -- the drawn via layers of this
route, in fabrication order.
- `label_layer` is declared ONLY where this stream actually puts
supply-relevant text: Metal1.pin (8/2) carries the pfet row's well-tap
PG pin text (one 'VDD_DIV' label), and Metal3.pin (30/2) carries
cmos5l_route.py's own per-net trunk labels -- the layer this deck's own
EXTRACTION_DECK.metal_labels reads -- including one 'VDD_DIV' and one
'VSS' each. Metal2 (10/2) carries no text in this GDS and is left
undeclared, matching the fleet precedent (gf180-drone-fc's
layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json declares label layers only where
its merged GDS puts PG text).
Layer-number provenance (dual-sourced, per #103's requirement -- IHP's
numbering differs from both gf180mcu and sky130, so nothing is copied
from another PDK's spec): every layer above is resolved from the PDK's
own libs.tech/klayout/tech/sg13cmos5l.lyp (Activ.drawing 1/0,
GatPoly.drawing 5/0, Cont.drawing 6/0, Metal1.drawing 8/0, Metal1.pin
8/2, Metal2.drawing 10/0, Via1.drawing 19/0, Via2.drawing 29/0,
Metal3.drawing 30/0, Metal3.pin 30/2, NWell.drawing 31/0, NWell.pin
31/2) AND cross-checked against klayout-tools' curated sg13cmos5l deck
layer table, which carries the identical pairs at this repo's own pinned
klt commit (layout/requirements.txt @ fdf04f71, deck file sha256
same hash the committed DRC/LVS record 20260830-204105-457cf5b cites for
its own deck): (1,0) Activ.drawing, (5,0) GatPoly.drawing, (6,0)
Cont.drawing, (8,0) Metal1.drawing, (8,2) Metal1.pin, (10,0)
Metal2.drawing, (19,0) Via1.drawing, (29,0) Via2.drawing, (30,0)
Metal3.drawing, (30,2) Metal3.pin, (31,0) NWell.drawing.
There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section here, and that is a recorded
disclosure, not an oversight. Declaring one was unsatisfiable at
curation time: klt erc's ties[] collapsed a real routed standard-cell
design into one electrical island and reported a FALSE erc.supply_short
-- filed upstream as klayout-tools#2169 (reproduced four ways in
gf180-drone-fc FRICTION F-034) and worked around here exactly as #103
directs. Because `ties[]` is omitted, `erc.missing_tie` is NOT COMPUTED
by this run (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted entirely ->
erc.missing_tie is never computed') -- a zero count in the committed
report is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, and must not
be cited as a well-tie verdict. The n-well-tap pin text of the committed
GDS is named as standing-in evidence below.
Two stale-at-curation facts, recorded for whoever re-runs this next:
(1) klayout-tools#2169 CLOSED upstream on 2026-09-20 (PR #2186 isolates
the tie connectivity graph from the wire/via graph), so a checked
`ties[]` read may be expressible at a newer klt pin than this repo's
layout pin -- re-check then; this spec keeps the #103 ruling.
(2) klt erc grades antenna ratios against a currently sky130-only limit
table, so on this PDK the antenna half of the report is honestly
`unchecked`/`not_checked` -- which is exactly why #103 and the upstream
item text grade the erc_findings rules, never the report's overall
`status` (klayout-tools#1994).
Standing-in well-tie evidence (what IS admissible, per the curated deck
and this record's own artifacts, while `erc.missing_tie` stays
uncomputed): the curated sg13cmos5l deck derives well ties as `nSD &
Activ & NWell` and substrate ties as `pSD & (Activ - NWell)` and reads
the well's own name from NWell.pin (31/2) (klayout-tools#1414):
- the pfet row is drawn inside ONE merged NWell (31/0) whose body is
tied by an nSD-covered Activ strip (7/0, inside that NWell), wired to
the VDD_DIV route -- compose.divider_chain.json pins it as
`divider_chain_pfet_w5_l0p5.nwell_tap` among VDD_DIV's 105 pins --
and labelled 'VDD_DIV' on NWell.pin (31/2) and Metal1.pin (8/2);
- the nfet row's body is tied by a pSD-covered Activ strip outside every
NWell, wired to the VSS route -- pinned as
`divider_chain_nfet_w2_l0p5.substrate_tap` among VSS's 89 pins;
- the same record's `lvs.divider_chain.json` compares the extracted
layout of this exact GDS against divider_chain.reference.spice
(status "match": 316/316 devices, 142/142 nets) and carries BOTH
supplies in its net_correspondence paired to reference-side nets
('VDD_DIV'->'VDD_DIV', 'VSS'->'VSS', pins), so the supplies were part
of the compare rather than absent from it -- the analog-column
demand the upstream item text adds on top of this spec's run.
